packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the work or author, or any earlier reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and the 16
image files of this packet (plus a file-name listing of the packet directory,
which showed a packet.json that I did not open). No web, search, catalogue or
edition was used. I do not identify work or author below.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
======================================================================

The packet shows two faces of one small upright leaf (ruler in overviews: about
11 cm wide), with sewing/binding holes along both long edges, clipped corners,
heavy foxing.

FACE 1 - overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002 (top left), image-003 (top
right), image-004 (middle left), image-005 (middle right), image-006 (lower
left), image-007 (lower right).
 - One column, long lines, upright orientation. About 27-28 lines of a small,
   very rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive in grey-brown ink occupy the upper
   ~45% of the face. The first line is cut by the top edge (text ran on from a
   lost or preceding area). The right ends of lines run to the very edge and
   some are slightly clipped.
 - No running title, no rubric, no colour, no enlarged initials inside the
   block. Paragraph breaks are marked only by short indents/gaps (tile
   image-002 lines 12 and 16; tile image-004 line 7).
 - Faint horizontal strokes run through the first three lines (tile image-002
   and image-003, lines 1-4). Observation: thin grey lines through the writing.
   Tentative interpretation: either drypoint/plummet ruling showing through or
   light cancellation; I cannot decide from the images.
 - One short word is struck through at the left of tile image-004 line 11.
 - Below the block, after a blank space, a single isolated line in a larger,
   more formal script with a large flourished initial E (tiles image-006 and
   image-007). The rest of the face (lower ~50%) is blank.
 - No interlinear or marginal glosses seen on this face.

FACE 2 - overview image-008.jpg; tiles image-009 (top left), image-010 (top
right), image-011 (middle left), image-012 (middle right), image-013 (lower
middle left), image-014 (lower middle right), image-015 (bottom left),
image-016 (bottom right).
 - Not a text page. Observation: scattered short entries in several sizes and
   at least two or three inks/hands, at different indents, with alphabets
   written out letter by letter, repeated single sentences, struck-through
   lines, smudged/wiped lines, large isolated capitals, diagonal pen strokes,
   and at the foot a set of three or four long hand-drawn horizontal lines
   carrying small hook- and dot-shaped marks, with a pen sketch at the right
   end. Tentative interpretation: pen trials / probationes pennae, including
   letter-address formulae and repeated sayings; the ruled lines with marks at
   the foot might be a rough staff with note-like signs or mere pen play - I
   cannot tell.
 - The very top line and the very bottom line are cut by the edges.

======================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED / LEFT UNREAD
======================================================================

Face 1: I attempted the whole block line by line (it is one continuous
passage, and the closing formal line). The script is extremely cursive; many
words are read from general shape only. Recognisable recurring words gave the
anchors: "loc(us)", "a diuisio(n)e", "membroru(m) diuide(n)ciu(m)",
"r(ati)o(n)alis / irr(ati)o(n)alis", "argume(n)tari", "(con)st(r)uctiue".
Everything between the anchors is low confidence and marked.
Face 2: all legible entries attempted; faint under-writing, wiped lines and
isolated letters are described rather than read.

Conventions: (..) = my proposed expansion of an abbreviation; (?) after a word
= uncertain reading of that word; [..] = short group I could not resolve;
[illegible] = longer unread stretch; | = no meaning, not used. Line numbers
are counted from the top of the named image; where a line continues from a
left tile into a right tile both labels are given.

======================================================================
3. FACE 1 - MAIN BLOCK
======================================================================

Tiles image-002 (left half of each line) and image-003 (right half); the two
overlap in the middle of the line, so the join word is given once.

image-002 L1 / image-003 L1 (top line, cut by the edge):
  [..]g[..] [illegible] vero(?) data(?) sed(?) [..] (con)stabiunt(ur)(?) q(uod)(?) illa(?) ma[..]ne(?) [..]

  [..] s(ecundu)m(?) ad a(n)i(m)al(?) e(st) r(ati)o(n)alis g(o)(?) ad a(n)i(m)al(?) e(st) irr(ati)o(n)alis q(ui)a arguit(ur) a [..]

  [..] sufficie(n)s(?) q(uod)(?) ly(?) semp(er)(?) p(ro) o(mn)ib(us)(?) semp(er)(?) solu(m)(?) s(ed)(?) p(ro)(?) [..] i(n) mala(?) [..]
image-002 L16 / image-003 L16 (begins with an indent):
  obuiat(?) aut(?) s(ed)(?) p(ar)tes(?) locu(m) a diuisi(on)e(?) p(ar)tes(?) st(?) q(uo)d mo(?)ue(n)t(?) [..]
image-002 L17 / image-003 L17 (bottom line of both tiles, partly cut):
  [..] e(st) i(n)diuid(u)ale(?) v(e)l i(n)diuid(u)ale(?) s(ed) n(on) o(mn)e(?) i(n)diuid(u)ale(?) [..]

Tiles image-004 (left) and image-005 (right). image-004 L1-L4 repeat
image-002 L14-L17 (overlap, same lines, not additional text); image-005 L1-L4
repeat image-003 L14-L17. New text begins at L5 of both tiles.

image-004 L5 / image-005 L5:
  i(n)diuiduo(?) aliq(?) aut(?) v(e)l aliu(m)(?) a(r)gume(n)tat(ur)(?) (con)tra(?) (et) n(on)(?) d(e)st(r)u(ct)i(u)e(?) ad d(e)st(ructionem)(?)
image-004 L6 / image-005 L6:
  a(n)i(m)alib(us)(?) al(?) q(ui)a n(on)(?) [..] s(ecundu)m(?) [..] n(on)(?) g(o)(?) al(?) i(n)diuid(u)ale(?) semp(er)(?) (con)tin[..](?)
image-004 L7 / image-005 L7 (begins with an indent):
  hac(?) sua(?) i(n) q(?) [..]atcia(?) q(uo)d a(?) al(?) n(on) e(st)(?) irr(ati)o(n)ale(?) [..] si(?)
image-004 L8 / image-005 L8:
  s(ed) e(st)(?) a(r)gume(n)ta(n)do oporteret s(i)c p(ro)ced(er)e(?) s(ed) o(mn)e(?) al(?) n(on)(?) d[..] s[..]

  ad al(?) [..] r(ati)o(n)ale v(e)l i(n)diuid[..](?) (con)s[..] (et) falsitas(?) s(i)c(?) (et) aliis(?) ex(?)

  [struck word] [..]u(m)(?) dicit(ur)(?) g(o)(?) loc(us) est(?) a diuisio(n)e i(n) aliis(?) d(i)u(i)de(n)tib(us)(?) (et) loc(us)(?) [..]

image-004 L15 / image-005 L15:
  o[..]nalit(er)(?) i(n) me(m)bris(?) diuide(n)tib(us)(?) p[..] sic(?) solui(?) a(r)gume(n)tu(m)(?) [..]
image-004 L16 / image-005 L16:
  (con)t(r)a(?) s(ecundu)m(?) diuisi(?) sic(?) i(n) diuisio(n)e(?) habe(n)t(?) ge(n)e(r)alita(te)m(?) sub(?) (con)sid(er)ac(ione)(?) i[..]
image-004 L17 / image-005 L17 (last line of the block; repeated at the top of
image-006 L2 and image-007 L2 - overlap, not additional text):
  [..] s(i)c(?) habet(?) diu(er)sitas(?) [..] diu(er)sis(?) loc(is)(?) q(uo)d(?) gen(er)al(i)t(er)(?) (con)ue(n)ie(n)t(er)(?) e[..]

Sense that I can observe without supplying words: the passage repeatedly names
a "locus a diuisione", "membra diuidentia", arguing "constructiue" and
(probably) "destructiue", with examples built on "rationalis / irrationalis"
and "animal" (abbreviated "al"); "asin(us)" at L9 is uncertain.

======================================================================
4. FACE 1 - ISOLATED CLOSING LINE (larger formal script)
======================================================================

image-006 L3 (left part: large looped initial E, crossed by two long diagonal
hairlines) continuing in image-007 L3:
  Et sic e(st) finis q(ui)nti(?) tractat(us)(?) hui[..]

Notes: "Et sic e(st) finis" is clear. The next word is short, begins with q
and carries an abbreviation stroke; "quinti" is my best reading but "quarti"
or another q-word cannot be excluded from the image. "tractat(us)" has a small
hole/blot in its last letters. The final word is cut by the right edge after
"hu" / "hui". Nothing follows on the face.

======================================================================
5. FACE 2 - PEN TRIALS (overview image-008.jpg)
======================================================================

Top area - image-009 (left) and image-010 (right):

image-009 L1 / image-010 L1 (cut by the top edge, darker ink):
  [..] d[..]tra(?) est(?) t(?) [..] ; further right isolated tall strokes and letters
image-009 L2 / image-010 L2 (an alphabet written out, letters spaced):
  g(?) h(?) i k k(?) l m n o p q [..]
image-009 L3 (left, beside the hole in the leaf):
  a [hole] mi(n)tas(?) arge(n)t(?) eiusd(em)(?)        [very uncertain; darker ink]

  It(em)(?) i(n)sunt(?) Anne(?) duo [..]obes(?)   then letters: d e f g h i k
image-009 L5 / image-010 L5:
  letters: m n o p q r(?) s(?) [tall s]   then: [..]ime(?) q(ui)nq(ue)(?) duo [..]obes(?)   then large pen-trial letters (g / B-like forms, a struck-through sign)
image-009 L6 / image-010 L6 (large initial O):
  O(mn)ia dat d(omi)n(u)s no(n) habet ergo(?) minus
image-009 L7 / image-010 L7:
  Op(er)a(?) n(ost)ra be(n)edicat v(ir)go maria
image-009 L8 / image-010 L8: a line that has been wiped/smudged and crossed
  through; I see only "J[..]" at the start and "habet(?)" at the end.
image-009 L9 / image-010 L9 (darker ink, begins with a large V and a paraph-
like stroke):
  Venerabili et reu(er)e(n)d(o)(?) p(at)ri(?) ac(?) viro d(omi)no d(omi)no
image-009 L10 / image-010 L10 (repeated at image-011 L2 / image-012 L2):
  he(n)rico(?) d[..] [..]ab[..](?) d(i)c(t)o(?) ba[..]re(?) d(i)c(t)o(?) [..]po(?) meo
image-011 L3 / image-012 L3 (ends in a heavy smudge):
  [..]issi(m)o(?) sincerissime(?) et sp[..]o(?) [smudged/wiped]

Middle area - image-011 (left) and image-012 (right):

image-011 L4: one large isolated word:  Sapie(n)s
image-012 (right of it, small, two short lines, the first begun with a struck

A long horizontal smear (wiped ink) crosses the leaf under these; under-writing

image-011 L6:  quicquid   [then isolated letters]  s t
image-011 L7 / image-012:  Ame(n)(?) [..]ssq(?) et vita(?)        [letters partly overwritten by a large pen-trial "B"/"ss" form]

  L6  [whole line struck through] Sp(er)auim(us)(?) [..]

image-015 L2 / image-016 L2:  Quicquid agas prudenter agas et respice
image-015 L3:  fine(m)

Foot - image-015 and image-016: three or four long hand-drawn horizontal
lines with small hooked marks, dots and two vertical bar-strokes placed on and
between them; at the right end a pen drawing of a tall staff with a flag- or
"B"-shaped appendage. Below the lowest line, cut by the bottom edge, a few
letters: "m[..]" and "h[..]". Not transcribed further.

======================================================================
6. LIMITATIONS
======================================================================

- Face 1 is in a hurried, highly abbreviated cursive; apart from the anchor
  words listed in section 2 and the closing line, every reading is tentative
  and should not be treated as a secure quotation. Word division and the
  resolution of "al" (possibly a(n)i(m)al) and of "g" (possibly (er)go) are
  my assumptions, shown in brackets.
- The first line of Face 1 is cut at the top; right-hand line ends are tight
  to the edge and a few final letters are lost; a hole interrupts image-003
  L6; stains cover parts of image-004 L5-L13.
- I could not decide whether the faint lines through Face 1 L1-L4 are ruling
  or deletion.
- Face 2 has overlapping layers (faint large letters under darker small
  entries); only the darker entries are read. The identity of the foot
  drawing/ruled lines is undetermined.
- Which face is recto and which verso cannot be told from the images.
- A wider view is not needed; a higher-magnification or raking-light image of
  Face 1 lines 1-12 and of the short word after "finis" in the closing line
  would be the most useful addition.
